eka-robotics-2026.tagline: A robot platform that picks and assembles wires 2.5x faster than humans

founders.background: Professor, MIT Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
founders.notable_achievement: Leading researcher in robot learning and reinforcement learning

eka-robotics-2026.team_highlights: The exact headcount has not been disclosed, but considering the Series A scale ($150M) and the stage of technology development, it is estimated at over 50 people. Both co-founders are globally recognized authorities in reinforcement learning-based robotic manipulation research.

product.summary: Eka Robotics is a robotic manipulation platform built on a Vision-Force-Action (VFA) model that achieves both generality and performance. By running reinforcement learning at scale in simulation to learn the laws of physics, it can reliably pick a wide variety of objects and insert wires at 2.5x human speed (1,500 operations per hour).
product.problem_statement: Existing industrial robots are specialized for single tasks and lack generality, while recent VLA (Vision-Language-Action) models can attempt a wide range of tasks but have low speed and accuracy, which limits their practical use. In particular, vision alone is insufficient for the final 1mm when grasping an object, making force/tactile feedback essential.
product.solution: The company combines a gripper with a proprietary built-in force sensor and a Vision-Force-Action (VFA) model, designed so the model directly uses force information at the moment of contact. Thousands of hours of robot experience are rapidly generated in a physics simulator, policies are learned through reinforcement learning, and the policies are then applied to real robots (sim-to-real).
key_features: 1,500 picks per hour (2.5x human rate)
Generalizes to objects and environments outside the training distribution
Capable of delicate tasks such as replacing light bulbs and inserting wires
Gripper unit cost under $1,000, with 5M-cycle durability
Detects force on contact to interact safely
product.tech_stack_or_innovation: The core is the Vision-Force-Action (VFA) model. While existing VLAs connect language, vision and action, Eka takes force as an input alongside vision and outputs actions. Sim-to-real gaps were overcome through simulation-based reinforcement learning, and the in-house force-sensing gripper is the hardware differentiator.
product.target_customer: Companies in manufacturing and logistics that perform pick-and-place and wire handling tasks. The company is currently running undisclosed pilots with several industrial customers.
product.business_model: Estimated to be a subscription or equipment sales model that bundles robot hardware (grippers) with software (VFA model and control systems). The exact pricing structure has not been disclosed.

direct_competitors.comparison: An open-source VLA model that emphasizes generality, but with lower manipulation speed and accuracy than Eka.
NVIDIA's robot foundation model, positioned between open-source and proprietary, but not specialized for force feedback.
Startups with their own VLA models, based on imitation learning, that cannot directly use force information, so Eka is likely to have an advantage in delicate tasks.

competitive_landscape.key_differentiator: The VFA model, which combines vision and force. Large-scale simulation-based reinforcement learning secures both generality and performance. In addition, through its in-house force-sensing gripper, the model directly learns physical interactions at the moment of contact.
competitive_landscape.moat: Fast iterative learning through physics simulation and reinforcement learning, tight integration with custom hardware, and accumulated sim-to-real technology are expected to widen the gap with competitors over time.
competitive_landscape.competitive_position_summary: Eka is regarded as the first commercial robotic manipulation platform to resolve the trade-off between generality and performance. Its force-based approach is an area that competing VLA models will find difficult to catch up with, and its $1.45B valuation reflects high market expectations.

trending_reason.summary: On October 20, 2026, Eka raised a $150M Series A round at a post-money valuation of $1.45B. The round was led by Andreessen Horowitz and F-Prime, with participation from Samsung Next and others. It is a historically large round for robotic manipulation, and investors are betting that Eka's VFA model could change the paradigm of industrial robots.
catalysts: $150M Series A raised on October 20, 2026 (lead: a16z, F-Prime)
Announced picking speed 2.5x faster than humans (1,500 per hour)
The VFA model using force feedback has drawn attention from industry experts
trending_reason.growth_metrics: Picking speed of 1,500 per hour (2.5x the human rate of 600), gripper unit cost under $1,000, 5M-cycle durability, and thousands of hours of environment experience generated within minutes in simulation.

nova-2026.tagline: A fintech that connects Brazilian credit card limits to Pix, enabling installment payments.

founders.notable_achievement: Co-founded Nova, former executive at Brazilian digital bank Neon

founders.background: Lead of Google Pay's Checkout API
founders.notable_achievement: Oversaw Google Pay Checkout API and is a payment infrastructure expert

founders.background: Former executive of Brazilian digital bank Neon
founders.notable_achievement: Co-founded Nova, former Neon executive

nova-2026.team_highlights: All three co-founders come from Brazilian fintech (Neon) and big tech (Google Pay). Currently operates with a lean team of 20.

product.summary: A digital wallet that lets consumers use their existing credit card limits to pay via Pix and Boleto in installments of up to 12 months. It describes itself as the 'operating system (OS)' for Brazil's payment system.
product.problem_statement: Brazil has both the world-class instant payment network Pix and an active credit card market, but the two are not connected at all. Pix is instantly free but offers no installments or credit benefits; credit cards are powerful but not accepted everywhere (such as Pix or Boleto bills).
product.solution: When a consumer registers an existing card in the Nova app, Nova becomes the 'merchant' for that card transaction, receives payment from the card issuer, and immediately pays the recipient via Pix or Boleto. Consumers enjoy credit card benefits (installments, points) while paying at non-card-accepting merchants.
key_features: Manage all existing credit cards in one app
Convert Pix and Boleto payments into credit card installments (up to 12 months)
AI-based fraud detection system
Integrate card limits via Open Finance
Recommend optimized payment methods tailored to consumers
product.tech_stack_or_innovation: Nova does not issue its own credit; it only uses existing card limits. It actively uses AI to collect recipient information from the web and social networks, building its own fraud detection model. The core technology is creating its own anti-fraud layer while relying on partner banks and card processors.
product.target_customer: Mainly individual customers and small businesses (SMBs) needing high-value, high-frequency payments. They use Nova for areas where credit cards are not well accepted, such as rent, tuition, and taxes.
product.business_model: Charges users transaction fees. Nova does not extend credit; all revenue comes from payment intermediation. It reported annual revenue of $12M (approx. KRW 6B).

competitive_landscape.key_differentiator: It does not issue its own credit but only connects existing card limits. This allows it to maintain a cooperative rather than competitive relationship with banks and card companies. It also combines Open Finance and AI to automatically recommend the optimal payment route for each user.
competitive_landscape.moat: An AI fraud detection model based on accumulated transaction data and the technical ability to reliably run the complex settlement process among merchants, banks, and card issuers. Even before the first product launch, it had processed over BRL 500M (approx. KRW 120B) in transactions, building up data.
competitive_landscape.competitive_position_summary: Positioning itself as the 'connecting layer' of Brazil's payment market, it precisely targets the gap between the two major infrastructures of Pix and credit cards. With lead investment from global VC Canaan, it has emerged as one of the most notable Series A companies in the Brazilian fintech ecosystem.

trending_reason.summary: Operating in stealth mode, it officially launched in November 2026 with a $24M Series A investment. With a clear value proposition of connecting Brazil's unique payment infrastructure (Pix + credit cards), it gained the most attention for having already achieved $12M in annual revenue before its official launch, validating traction.
catalysts: November 2026: $24M Series A raise and end of stealth mode
Explosive growth of Brazil's instant payment network Pix increases demand for card connectivity
Expansion of Open Finance improves fintech data accessibility
trending_reason.growth_metrics: Over 300K cumulative downloads, cumulative transaction volume exceeding BRL 500M (approx. KRW 120B). Monthly growth rate above 20%. Already profitable at the operating level.

market_outlook.tam_sam_som: Brazil's credit card market was approx. BRL 250B in 2025, and Pix daily transaction volume exceeds 200M. TAM is the entire Brazilian payment market (hundreds of billions of dollars), SAM is the Pix/Boleto payment market where credit cards are not used (tens of billions of dollars). SOM targets Brazilian small and medium businesses and high-value individual consumers.
market_outlook.market_trend: Since the introduction of Pix by the Central Bank of Brazil, instant payments have exploded. At the same time, Open Finance regulations have allowed third-party fintechs to access financial data, facilitating the emergence of intermediary services like Nova.
market_outlook.growth_potential: Currently, there are about 200M credit cards issued in Brazil, but most of their limits are unused and idle in modern payment methods like Pix. If these limits were connected, the market size could grow exponentially.
risks: Changes in Brazilian payment regulations (e.g., introduction of Pix fees)
Launch of competing services by large banks or card companies (Visa, Mastercard)
High fraud risk (chargeback and fraud potential for credit card-based Pix payments)
Brazilian macroeconomic uncertainty and interest rate fluctuations
market_outlook.risk_mitigation: Manages risk with an AI-based fraud detection model. Adopts a strategy of treating banks/card companies as partners, not competitors. Has already passed break-even at the operating level, ensuring financial sustainability.

nova-2026.editor_pick_comment: It precisely targets the gap of 'connection failure' between already advanced payment infrastructures. Entering profitability with a 20-person team not only shows growth potential but also proves business model efficiency.

product.summary: Develops an RNA therapy that delivers an ASO (antisense oligonucleotide) targeting microRNA-204 (miR-204) via intra-articular injection to halt osteoarthritis progression and regenerate cartilage.
product.problem_statement: Osteoarthritis affects over 500 million people worldwide; current treatments only provide pain relief or anti-inflammatory effects, with no disease-modifying therapy that regenerates cartilage.
product.solution: miR-204 is a key microRNA that promotes chondrocyte senescence, driving osteoarthritis. Lifleks Science develops an ASO targeting miR-204 (injectable LF-ASO-001) to create a disease-modifying osteoarthritis drug (DMOAD) that simultaneously protects cartilage and relieves pain with a single intra-articular injection.
key_features: Selectively degrades miR-204-5p to inhibit chondrocyte senescence
Unique mechanism destabilizing the AGO2 protein-RNA complex
Sustained efficacy with a single intra-articular injection (confirmed in mouse models)
Achieves analgesic effects comparable to existing pain relievers along with structural protection
Favorable preclinical safety profile (no articular or systemic toxicity)
product.tech_stack_or_innovation: A chemically optimized ASO displaces the 3' end of miR-204-5p in the AGO2 PAZ domain, destabilizing the complex and degrading the microRNA—a proprietary mechanism designed via molecular dynamics simulations and validated in vitro/in vivo.
product.target_customer: Patients aged 50+ with degenerative osteoarthritis, particularly knee osteoarthritis
product.business_model: Pipeline-based drug development: after LF-ASO-001 enters clinical trials, technology transfer or co-development; expand the same platform to obesity, kidney, and heart diseases for multi-pipeline value creation.

direct_competitors.name: Merck KGaA (no commercial stage)
direct_competitors.comparison: The most advanced clinical-stage drug in the osteoarthritis DMOAD space, but no DMOAD has been approved yet; Lifleks' RNA-based mechanism is fundamentally different.

competitive_landscape.moat: Proprietary ASO design based on miR-204-AGO2 complex destabilization (original patents), 20 years of Prof. Jin-Hong Kim's osteoarthritis and RNA biology research, and disease mechanism studies published in Cell Metabolism provide a scientific foundation for pipeline expansion.

product.summary: IMIO has developed a powdered product made from freeze-dried microorganisms (bacteria, fungi, and yeast). When applied to crop residue left after harvest, the product accelerates decomposition, and the released nutrients are absorbed by the next crop. This reduces the use of chemical fertilizers and lowers farmers' cultivation costs.
product.problem_statement: Farmers struggle to manage crop residue such as stalks and stubble left after harvest. Natural decomposition is slow, and nutrients are lost. As a result, additional fertilizer is required, and removing or tilling residue physically adds cost. Modern crop varieties also have higher lignin content, which makes decomposition more difficult. Existing microbial products have failed to earn farmers' trust, as microbial survival rates during storage or application are low and their effects are inconsistent.
product.solution: IMIO cultivates each microbial strain separately, freeze-dries them, and activates them with water immediately before use. This approach provides a shelf life of more than 12 months and delivers maximum active microorganisms at the time of application. The product is sold under the Re-Gen brand in two versions: one for grain crops such as corn, and one for horticultural crops such as broccoli. Farmers can use their existing equipment as is.
key_features: Precise blending through separate cultivation of each strain
Maximized survival rate through freeze-drying
Activation with water immediately before application
Storable at room temperature for more than 12 months
Two versions: 'Re-Gen for Row Crops' for grain crops such as corn, and 'Re-Gen for Produce' for horticultural crops such as broccoli
product.tech_stack_or_innovation: Each microbial strain is cultivated separately and mixed in precise ratios, and lyophilization (freeze-drying) minimizes damage during the drying process. product.target_customer: Large-scale grain farms (especially corn) in the U.S. Midwest, and horticultural farms growing broccoli, lettuce, and other produce

product.summary: A B2B security platform that inserts imperceptible digital watermarks in real-time into all audio generated by AI voice agents, allowing the receiving end to verify them. 32-64 bit payload embedding individual agent identification information and permissions
On-premises deployment option that can run within customer infrastructure
